questions.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4$ for $x\le 0.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents one-half of the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14251855/assets/de9f30a4f54875e05a8cedb6c73af37ad7146c56ab62d0b2b2d3f3fa359160ca.png)

 

As a result, we obtain that in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{3\pi }{2},\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}+(\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2} \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ+{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ) \\  & ={\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}{sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{\pi /2}^{3\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{4}{sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=4.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $2$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 2,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}x\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2}{\rho }^{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

The region $R$ is enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=2.$
Express the following triple integral in spherical polar coordinates. 

$$
{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $\sqrt{2}$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le \sqrt{2},\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)^{2}\cdot \rho  \\  & ={\rho }^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain  

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}{x}^{2}\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}{\rho }^{3}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{2}⁡ϕ\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{\sqrt{2}}{\rho }^{5}{cos}^{2}⁡\theta {sin}^{3}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}3{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3/2}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=1.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $1$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 1,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=3{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3/2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =3{e}^{({\rho }^{2})^{3/2}} \\  & =3{e}^{{\rho }^{3}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}3{e}^{({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2})^{3}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}3{e}^{{\rho }^{3}}\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{1}3{\rho }^{2}{e}^{{\rho }^{3}}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{1}3{\rho }^{2}{e}^{{\rho }^{3}}\,d\rho  \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot [{e}^{{\rho }^{3}}]_{\rho =0}^{\rho =1}\,d\rho  \\  & =-(-1-1)\cdot (2\pi -0)\cdot ({e}^{1}-{e}^{0}) \\  & =2\cdot 2\pi \cdot (e-1) \\  & =4\pi (e-1)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Evaluate the triple integral

$$
{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V
$$

over the region $R$ enclosed inside the sphere ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}=16.$
questions.worked_solution:
We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∭}_{R}f(x,y,z)\,dV={∭}_{Δ}\,f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\,{\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ.
$$

If $(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)$ are the spherical coordinates of a point, then its Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ can be found by using the following formulas:

$$
x=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,y=\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\,z=\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ
$$

Notice that the region $R$ represents the sphere of radius $4$ centered at the origin. 
As a result, in spherical polar coordinates, our region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ=\{(\rho ,\theta ,ϕ)\,:\,0\le \rho \le 4,\,0\le \theta \le 2\pi ,\,0\le ϕ\le \pi \}.
$$

Next, we substitute the spherical polar coordinates into the function $f(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & =f(\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ,\rho \operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ) \\  & =\frac{1}{\rho }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the change of variables formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}\frac{1}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}}}\,\text{d}V & ={∭}_{Δ}\frac{1}{\rho }\cdot {\rho }^{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }{\int }_{0}^{2\pi }{\int }_{0}^{4}\rho \operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,d\rho \,d\theta \,dϕ \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\,dϕ\cdot {\int }_{0}^{2\pi }d\theta \cdot {\int }_{0}^{4}\rho \,d\rho  \\  & =[-\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ]_{ϕ=0}^{ϕ=\pi }\cdot [\theta ]_{\theta =0}^{\theta =2\pi }\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{\rho }^{2}]}_{\rho =0}^{\rho =4}\,d\rho  \\  & =-(-1-1)\cdot (2\pi -0)\cdot \frac{1}{2}(16-0) \\  & =2\cdot 2\pi \cdot 8 \\  & =32\pi \end{aligned}
$$
